chosen.classifier: average over all 6 base classifiers (b-kde, knn, svm, nn, rf, Adaboost.M1) as printed; no per-classifier per-dataset table
chosen.condition: original IR datasets, oversampled to balance; 10 rounds of 10-fold CV

summary_rows.label: Wilcoxon p-value CGMOS vs SMOTE (Table 4): Knn / Rf / B-kde / Nn / Svm / Boost

outcome.stat_test: Wilcoxon signed-ranks test, CGMOS vs each compared method per classifier (Table 4, p.5, printed 1627); paper states all p < 0.05

win_claim.quote: The paper provides a proof that the proposed algorithm is guaranteed to work better than SMOTE for training data. Further, experimental results on 30 real-world datasets show that CGMOS works better than existing algorithms when using 6 different classifiers.

uncertain: No per-dataset per-classifier results; G-mean only aggregate (Table 2, p.6/printed 1628), so chosen metric is AUC averaged over 6 classifiers (Table 3, p.7/printed 1629)
how_obtained 'not stated' for all: binarization rule given (least-populated class vs rest) but not which datasets were multi-class (p.4/printed 1626)
Table 1 'UKnowledge' vs Table 3 'UserKnowledge' name mismatch (p.5 vs p.7)
Statlog and ImgSeg have identical S#/F#/R/Year in Table 1 (2310/19/0.17/1990); which Statlog variant is not stated (p.5)
Chess R printed 0.91 and BreastCancer 0.53, QSAR 0.51 (#minority/#majority) copied as printed (p.5)
best_other excludes CGMOS and SMOTE; computed as max of the other 6 printed columns
Author list in PDF is Zhang, Ma, Gan, Jiang, Agam (IIT), not 'Zhang & Li' as in task key (p.1)
notes: CIKM 2016. Tables read from rendered page images at 200 dpi (text layer column-scrambled). Table 3 bold marks copied. Table 2 Gscore defined as sqrt(Precision*Recall) per class (p.5), reported separately for minority and majority. Classifiers: b-kde, knn, svm (RBF), nn, rf (C4.5), Adaboost.M1. Extra experiment on oversampling amount k*delta (Fig. 3) is plots only. No supplementary material or GitHub referenced.
